blind_target.title: Interpersonal movement synchrony facilitates pro-social behavior in childrens peer-play.
blind_target.evidence_quote: As such, Tunçgenç & Cohen’s (2016b) measurement of social bonding behaviors will be employed to determine if the results can be replicated in the current study.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Despite findings from Tunçgenç & Cohen (2016b), the results from the current study reveal that interpersonal synchrony does not lead to increased instrumental helping and social bonding behaviors in three- to five-year-old children when paired with an adult partner.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast the absence of the central helping/social-bonding effect with the target. Limitations and exploratory empathy analyses do not replace that verdict.

luna_triage.reason: The source states that it uses the Tunçgenç and Cohen 2016b social-bonding measures to determine whether their results replicate in this study. It reports the original finding as increased instrumental helping and social bonding, and directly compares its outcomes against that finding. Reference entry 2016b is the cited Developmental Science paper with DOI 10.1111/desc.12505. The shipped Kirschner and Tomasello 2010 paper concerns joint music making and is a distinct original, not this finding.
